record.title: Report of the Auditor-General on the Accounts of the Botswana Government for the Year Ended 31 March 2019
record.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session. Section VIII 'Local Government Authorities' (p.91-92, para 117) names every audited council: 'In terms of Section 68 (3) of the Local Government Act, (Cap 40:01) and Section 32 (3) of the Tribal Land Regulations (Tribal Land Act, (Cap 32:02), I am required to audit the accounts of all Councils and Land Boards... The Local Government authorities under the scope of my mandate are as follows: Town and City Councils — City of Francistown Council, Gaborone City Council, Jwaneng Town Council, Lobatse Town Council, Selibe Phikwe Town Council, Sowa Town Council; District Councils — Central District Council, Chobe District Council, Ghanzi District Council, Kgalagadi District Council, Kgatleng District Council, Kweneng District Council, North East District Council, North West District Council, South East District Council, Southern District Council.' The same report also finds (p.75) that '[a]lthough the Department had made financial provision of P23 246 480 in the Estimates of Expenditure for 2017/18 for the payment of Government's contribution to the Gaborone City Council in lieu of rates on its rateable properties in the Council area, this money was never paid over to the Council in that year' -- a direct, named-council law-to-practice pairing with the Local Government Act's grant-in-lieu-of-rates provision. It further documents (p.14, Housing Fund section) named-council remittances and shortfalls to a national Housing Fund (established by Housing Fund Order, S.I. No. 51 of 2015), e.g. 'confirmation of remittances to the Fund had been submitted by the undernoted Councils but had not been captured on the accounts: Central District Council 11 542 823.72, City of Francistown 510 361.10, Gaborone City Council 12 363 955.83', noting that 'in all the years since inception in 2015 no expenditures had been incurred from the Fund'.
record.cadence_note: Part of an annual Auditor-General reporting series naming all Councils; the near-identical enumeration recurs in the 2019-2020 edition (bw-auditor-general-report-2019-2020). No working link to a subsequent edition (FY2020-21 or later) was located this session.

record.title: Report of the Auditor-General on the Accounts of the Botswana Government for the Year Ended 31 March 2020
record.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session. Section XI 'Local Government Authorities' (p.92-93, para 77) repeats the full named-council enumeration in near-identical wording to the 2018-2019 edition: 'In terms of Section 68 (3) of the Local Government Act, (Cap 40:01)... I am required to audit the accounts of all Councils and Land Boards... Town and City Councils — City of Francistown Council, Gaborone City Council, Jwaneng Town Council, Lobatse Town Council, Selibe Phikwe Town Council, Sowa Town Council; District Councils — Central District Council, Chobe District Council, Ghanzi District Council, Kgalagadi District Council, Kgatleng District Council, Kweneng District Council, North East District Council, North West District Council, South East District Council, Southern District Council.' It also documents specific named-council fund flows: on the Day Care Centre Programme (p.42), '[t]he Day Care Centre Programme under the Department of Pre and Primary Education disburses funds to District Councils through the Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development. The District Councils then disburse the funds to Day Care Centres run or administered by NGOs.' On drought relief (pp.49-51, item 48), 'the North West District Council constructed a clinic, LA2 house, public toilets, guard house, and also installed water tanks at Nxaraga at a cost of P872 128.01', and separately that '[t]he Ministry through different district councils had diverted P4.6 million from the Ipelegeng account, to finance other projects identified under Self Help Housing Agency (SHHA) Programme'. On social-protection payments infrastructure (p.51), 'an amount of P65 408 332 was paid to South East District Council as refund for unclaimed benefits for all Councils' -- a named-council figure tied to the Smart Switch beneficiary-card payment system.

record.title: Report of the Auditor-General on the Accounts of the Botswana Government for the Financial Year Ended 31 March 2021
record.description: VERIFIED GENUINE via raw curl this session (HTTP 200, content-type application/pdf, ~4MB, 221 pages -- ruled out both a 404 and a WebFetch hallucination, see _dropped for why that check mattered). Transmittal letter (p.2): 'In accordance with Section 124 (3) of the Constitution of Botswana, I have the honour to submit my report on the audit of the accounts of the Government for the financial year ended 31 March 2021. ... Pulane D. Letebele AUDITOR GENERAL', dated 08 November 2022. Section IX 'Local Government Authorities' (p.99, para 104) repeats the same statutory-mandate wording as the 2018-2019 and 2019-2020 editions and names the same sixteen councils: 'In terms of Section 68 (3) of the Local Government Act, (Cap 40:01) and Tribal Land Act, (Cap 32:02) and Section 32 (3) of the Tribal Land Regulations, I am required to audit the accounts of all Councils and Land Boards... My audit findings across all Local Authorities revealed very low collection of Income from Own Sources as laid down in the Charts of Accounts. Rates and SHHA debtors continue to increase annually as demonstrated in tables below.' The Debtors for Rates table (p.99, urban councils, 2020/2021 figures, Pula) reads: 'Francistown 119 483 535 / Gaborone 460 224 528 / Jwaneng 14 420 755 / Lobatse 18 713 748 / Selebi Phikwe 14 754 688 / Sowa 190 768 / Total 627 788 022'. The Debtors for SHHA/BML table (p.100, all ten district councils, 2020/2021 figures, Pula) reads: 'Central 182 600 954 / Chobe 16 530 198 / Ghanzi 11 254 631 / Kgalagadi 513 524 / Kgatleng 36 780 396 / Kweneng 117 164 454 / North East 42 778 790 / North West 13 577 898 / South East 21 324 591 / Southern 10 500 114 / Total 453 025 550'. Both tables present 2018/2019, 2019/2020, and 2020/2021 figures side-by-side for all sixteen councils, i.e. this report's own text independently restates the prior two years' audited rates/SHHA-debtor figures alongside the new year (see dependencies for the resulting uses_data_from edge to bw-auditor-general-report-2019-2020).
record.cadence_note: Third consecutive edition in the same annual Auditor-General series as bw-auditor-general-report-2018-2019 and bw-auditor-general-report-2019-2020, and more recent than either -- fills the gap the prior AF/G.23 round left open ('No working link to a subsequent edition (FY2020-21 or later) was located this session'). Notably, gov.bw's own official audit-report index (https://www.gov.bw/business-compliance/accessing-government-audit-reports) lists editions only up to 2018-2019, so this genuinely-hosted FY2020-2021 PDF is not discoverable via that index -- it was found via direct URL only. No working link to a FY2021-2022 or FY2022-2023 edition was located this session either; see _dropped.

record.title: Report of the Auditor-General for the Year Ended 31 March 2020
record.publisher: Office of the Auditor-General, Kingdom of Lesotho
record.description: Names Maseru District Council (MDC) and its constituent community councils with specific Maloti figures. On unused road-maintenance funds (s.15.5.2(a)): "It was established that in the financial year 2017/18 Maseru District Council had a budget for maintenance/rehabilitation of Mahloenyeng-Matsieng and Seng-Setala Roads, funds were received in the second quarter but were not utilized at the end of the financial year. For example, Mahloenyeng-Matsieng Road was budgeted M1,012,000 for tools and equipment and Seng-Setala had a budget of M1,125,000 for blasting, that were not utilised." On the thinly-spread Development Fund (s.15.5.2(b)): "The Development Fund had to be spread across all the development projects in the different community councils, thereby giving each community council limited funds." Table 15.5.2 (sourced "MDC records") gives year-by-year Maloti allocations by named road project, e.g. "Mahloenyeng Matsieng 42km ... 2017/18 M4,421,707 / 2018/19 M2,191,058 / 2019/20 M1,547,400 ... Still in Progress," with further rows for Hata-Butle-Tloutle (12km), Matsieng-Nkesi (72km), and Seng-Setala (87km). This is the clearest direct evidence in this round of a central Development Fund being distributed by/through a District Council to named community-council-level road projects, with the audit explicitly attributing under-completion to over-thin spreading of funds.
record.cadence_note: Annual statutory audit report; this is the FY ended 31 March 2020 edition of a recurring series (see also the FY2021, FY2022, and FY2024 editions elsewhere in this corpus).

record.title: Report of the Auditor-General for the Year Ended 31 March 2022
record.publisher: Office of the Auditor-General, Kingdom of Lesotho
record.description: Documents an intra-local-government reimbursement dependency at Leribe District Council (LDC), with a cleanly-extracted unaccounted-funds figure (s.12.2.2(a), "No loss reports prepared - M279,200"): "Employees of the Leribe District Council (LDC) are required to complete cash withdrawal slips when claiming out-of-pocket expenses for items such as lunch, soft drinks, office calling cards, individual airtime, electricity units, and transportation related to office duties. These expenses are reimbursed by the Community Councils, Urban Councils, and District Council Secretaries (DCS) offices," and "approved withdrawals totalled M33,738 while the bank statements reflected withdrawals amounting to M312,938. As a result, there was an unaccounted amount of M279,200." The finding cites Treasury Regulations 2014 §§81, 85 and Local Government Service Act 2008 §32(1)(b) as its legal basis (see ls-local-government-service-act-2008 for a caveat on the Act's own Section-85 citation elsewhere in this report).
record.cadence_note: Annual statutory audit report; this is the FY ended 31 March 2022 edition of a recurring series (see also the FY2020, FY2021, and FY2024 editions elsewhere in this corpus).

record.title: National Audit Office — Audit Report on the Accounts of the Rodrigues Regional Assembly, 2014
record.description: Section 2.5.1 "Financial Allocation to RRA" (page 9): "In September 2013, Government approved a budget allocation to RRA in the sum of Rs 1,950 million, comprising Rs 1,550 million for recurrent grant and Rs 400 million for capital grant. The actual amount of grant received was Rs 2,170,913,800, including an amount of Rs 220,913,800 as additional contribution from the Programme 311- 'Rodrigues Development' of the Prime Minister's Office. Revenue collected by the RRA amounted to Rs 25,356,042, thus bringing total revenue to Rs 2,196,269,842." This documents RRA's FY2014 revenue as roughly 99% central-government grant (Rs 2,170,913,800 of Rs 2,196,269,842 total), compositely sourced from a general Government budget allocation plus a specifically named Prime Minister's Office programme line (Programme 311, "Rodrigues Development").
record.cadence_note: Annual audit report (FY2014 edition); part of NAO's dedicated Rodrigues Regional Assembly report series (confirmed via NAO's own audit-report index — see _dropped).

record.title: National Audit Office — Audit Report on the Accounts of the Rodrigues Regional Assembly, 2019-20
record.description: Section 2.3 "Rodrigues Consolidated Fund (RCF) - Transfer from RCF to cater for Shortfall" (page 14): "RRA received a grant of some Rs 3,898 million from the Central Government in 2019-20. Revenue totalling some Rs 38 million were collected by the RRA, bringing the total inflow to some Rs 3,936 million. Total expenditure for 2019-20 amounted to Rs 3,955 million. Some Rs 20.9 million were transferred from RCF to cater for the shortfall." A three-year "Government Grant" comparison table in the same section: "3,681,490,778 [2019-20] / 3,575,000,000 [2018-19] / 3,425,000,000 [2017-18]" with corresponding "Additional Contribution 216,490,000 / 30,000,000 / -". Section 4.2, "Detailed Statement of Revenue of the Rodrigues Consolidated Fund" (Table 4, in Rs million): "Government Grant 3,897.98 [2019-20] / 3,605.00 [2018-19] / 3,425.00 [2017-18]," with: "Revenue of the RRA comprises principally of Grants/Contributions from the Central Government and internally generated revenue which consists of receipts from licence fees, social contributions, property income, sales of goods and services, incidental sales by non-market establishment, miscellaneous sales of goods and services, fines and miscellaneous revenue." CAVEAT: the report itself flags an internal accounting inconsistency — "An inconsistent accounting treatment of the item 'Grant - Contribution from Central Government'... The total Grants figure was wrongly stated as Rs 3,918,936,526" — a Rs 20,955,748 discrepancy between how the grant vs. RCF-transfer figures were classified in RRA's own accounts that year; the exact-rupee Table 2 figure (Rs 3,681,490,778) and the Table 4 Rs-million figure (3,897.98M, which appears inclusive of the Additional Contribution) do not reconcile cleanly and both should be treated as reported by the auditors rather than as a single unambiguous total.
record.cadence_note: Annual audit report (FY2019-20 edition, includes FY2018-19 and FY2017-18 comparatives); part of NAO's dedicated Rodrigues Regional Assembly report series (confirmed via NAO's own audit-report index — see _dropped).
